text.KJV: The song of songs, which is Solomon's.
text.ASV: The Song of songs, which is Solomon's.
text.WEB: The Song of songs, which is Solomon’s.

text.KJV: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth: for thy love is better than wine.
text.ASV: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth; For thy love is better than wine.
text.WEB: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth; for your love is better than wine.

text.KJV: Because of the savour of thy good ointments thy name is as ointment poured forth, therefore do the virgins love thee.
text.ASV: Thine oils have a goodly fragrance; Thy name is `as' oil poured forth; Therefore do the virgins love thee.
text.WEB: Your oils have a pleasing fragrance. Your name is oil poured out, therefore the virgins love you.

text.KJV: Draw me, we will run after thee: the king hath brought me into his chambers: we will be glad and rejoice in thee, we will remember thy love more than wine: the upright love thee.
text.ASV: Draw me; we will run after thee: The king hath brought me into his chambers; We will be glad and rejoice in thee; We will make mention of thy love more than of wine: Rightly do they love thee.
text.WEB: Take me away with you. Let us hurry. The king has brought me into his rooms. Friends We will be glad and rejoice in you. We will praise your love more than wine! Beloved They are right to love you.

text.KJV: I am black, but comely, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, as the tents of Kedar, as the curtains of Solomon.
text.ASV: I am black, but comely, Oh ye daughters of Jerusalem, As the tents of Kedar, As the curtains of Solomon.
text.WEB: I am dark, but lovely, you daughters of Jerusalem, like Kedar’s tents, like Solomon’s curtains.

text.KJV: Look not upon me, because I am black, because the sun hath looked upon me: my mother's children were angry with me; they made me the keeper of the vineyards; but mine own vineyard have I not kept.
text.ASV: Look not upon me, because I am swarthy, Because the sun hath scorched me. My mother's sons were incensed against me; They made me keeper of the vineyards; `But' mine own vineyard have I not kept.
text.WEB: Don’t stare at me because I am dark, because the sun has scorched me. My mother’s sons were angry with me. They made me keeper of the vineyards. I haven’t kept my own vineyard.

text.KJV: Tell me, O thou whom my soul loveth, where thou feedest, where thou makest thy flock to rest at noon: for why should I be as one that turneth aside by the flocks of thy companions?
text.ASV: Tell me, O thou whom my soul loveth, Where thou feedest `thy flock', Where thou makest `it' to rest at noon: For why should I be as one that is veiled Beside the flocks of thy companions?
text.WEB: Tell me, you whom my soul loves, where you graze your flock, where you rest them at noon; For why should I be as one who is veiled beside the flocks of your companions?

text.KJV: If thou know not, O thou fairest among women, go thy way forth by the footsteps of the flock, and feed thy kids beside the shepherds' tents.
text.ASV: If thou know not, O thou fairest among women, Go thy way forth by the footsteps of the flock, And feed thy kids beside the shepherds' tents.
text.WEB: If you don’t know, most beautiful among women, follow the tracks of the sheep. Graze your young goats beside the shepherds’ tents.

text.KJV: I have compared thee, O my love, to a company of horses in Pharaoh's chariots.
text.ASV: I have compared thee, O my love, To a steed in Pharaoh's chariots.
text.WEB: I have compared you, my love, to a steed in Pharaoh’s chariots.

text.KJV: Thy cheeks are comely with rows of jewels, thy neck with chains of gold.
text.ASV: Thy cheeks are comely with plaits `of hair', Thy neck with strings of jewels.
text.WEB: Your cheeks are beautiful with earrings, your neck with strings of jewels.

text.KJV: We will make thee borders of gold with studs of silver.
text.ASV: We will make thee plaits of gold With studs of silver.
text.WEB: We will make you earrings of gold, with studs of silver.

text.KJV: While the king sitteth at his table, my spikenard sendeth forth the smell thereof.
text.ASV: While the king sat at his table, My spikenard sent forth its fragrance.
text.WEB: While the king sat at his table, my perfume spread its fragrance.

text.KJV: A bundle of myrrh is my well-beloved unto me; he shall lie all night betwixt my breasts.
text.ASV: My beloved is unto me `as' a bundle of myrrh, That lieth betwixt my breasts.
text.WEB: My beloved is to me a sachet of myrrh, that lies between my breasts.

text.KJV: My beloved is unto me as a cluster of camphire in the vineyards of Engedi.
text.ASV: My beloved is unto me `as' a cluster of henna-flowers In the vineyards of En-gedi.
text.WEB: My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms from the vineyards of En Gedi.

text.KJV: Behold, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair; thou hast doves' eyes.
text.ASV: Behold, thou art fair, my love; Behold thou art fair; Thine eyes are `as' doves.
text.WEB: Behold, you are beautiful, my love. Behold, you are beautiful. Your eyes are doves.

text.KJV: Behold, thou art fair, my beloved, yea, pleasant: also our bed is green.
text.ASV: Behold, thou art fair, my beloved, yea, pleasant: Also our couch is green.
text.WEB: Behold, you are beautiful, my beloved, yes, pleasant; and our couch is verdant.

text.KJV: The beams of our house are cedar, and our rafters of fir.
text.ASV: The beams of our house are cedars, `And' our rafters are firs.
text.WEB: The beams of our house are cedars. Our rafters are firs.

text.KJV: I am the rose of Sharon, and the lily of the valleys.
text.ASV: I am a rose of Sharon, A lily of the valleys.
text.WEB: I am a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valleys.

text.KJV: As the lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.
text.ASV: As a lily among thorns, So is my love among the daughters.
text.WEB: As a lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.

text.KJV: As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, and his fruit was sweet to my taste.
text.ASV: As the apple-tree among the trees of the wood, So is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, And his fruit was sweet to my taste.
text.WEB: As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, his fruit was sweet to my taste.

text.KJV: He brought me to the banqueting house, and his banner over me was love.
text.ASV: He brought me to the banqueting-house, And his banner over me was love.
text.WEB: He brought me to the banquet hall. His banner over me is love.

text.KJV: Stay me with flagons, comfort me with apples: for I am sick of love.
text.ASV: Stay ye me with raisins, refresh me with apples; For I am sick from love.
text.WEB: Strengthen me with raisins, refresh me with apples; For I am faint with love.

text.KJV: His left hand is under my head, and his right hand doth embrace me.
text.ASV: His left hand `is' under my head, And his right hand doth embrace me.
text.WEB: His left hand is under my head. His right hand embraces me.

text.KJV: I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please.
text.ASV: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, By the roes, or by the hinds of the field, That ye stir not up, nor awake `my' love, Until he please.
text.WEB: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, or by the hinds of the field, that you not stir up, nor awaken love, until it so desires.

text.KJV: The voice of my beloved! behold, he cometh leaping upon the mountains, skipping upon the hills.
text.ASV: The voice of my beloved! behold, he cometh, Leaping upon the mountains, Skipping upon the hills.
text.WEB: The voice of my beloved! Behold, he comes, leaping on the mountains, skipping on the hills.

text.KJV: My beloved is like a roe or a young hart: behold, he standeth behind our wall, he looketh forth at the windows, shewing himself through the lattice.
text.ASV: My beloved is like a roe or a young hart: Behold, he standeth behind our wall; He looketh in at the windows; He glanceth through the lattice.
text.WEB: My beloved is like a roe or a young deer. Behold, he stands behind our wall! He looks in at the windows. He glances through the lattice.

text.KJV: My beloved spake, and said unto me, Rise up, my love, my fair one, and come away.
text.ASV: My beloved spake, and said unto me, Rise up, my love, my fair one, and come away.
text.WEB: My beloved spoke, and said to me, “Rise up, my love, my beautiful one, and come away.

text.KJV: For, lo, the winter is past, the rain is over and gone;
text.ASV: For, lo, the winter is past; The rain is over and gone;
text.WEB: For, behold, the winter is past. The rain is over and gone.

text.KJV: The flowers appear on the earth; the time of the singing of birds is come, and the voice of the turtle is heard in our land;
text.ASV: The flowers appear on the earth; The time of the singing `of birds' is come, And the voice of the turtle-dove is heard in our land;
text.WEB: The flowers appear on the earth. The time of the singing has come, and the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land.

text.KJV: The fig tree putteth forth her green figs, and the vines with the tender grape give a good smell. Arise, my love, my fair one, and come away.
text.ASV: The fig-tree ripeneth her green figs, And the vines are in blossom; They give forth their fragrance. Arise, my love, my fair one, and come away.
text.WEB: The fig tree ripens her green figs. The vines are in blossom. They give out their fragrance. Arise, my love, my beautiful one, and come away.”

text.KJV: O my dove, that art in the clefts of the rock, in the secret places of the stairs, let me see thy countenance, let me hear thy voice; for sweet is thy voice, and thy countenance is comely.
text.ASV: O my dove, that art in the clefts of the rock, In the covert of the steep place, Let me see thy countenance, Let me hear thy voice; For sweet is thy voice, and thy countenance is comely.
text.WEB: My dove in the clefts of the rock, In the hiding places of the mountainside, Let me see your face. Let me hear your voice; for your voice is sweet, and your face is lovely.

text.KJV: Take us the foxes, the little foxes, that spoil the vines: for our vines have tender grapes.
text.ASV: Take us the foxes, the little foxes, That spoil the vineyards; For our vineyards are in blossom.
text.WEB: Catch for us the foxes, the little foxes that plunder the vineyards; for our vineyards are in blossom.

text.KJV: My beloved is mine, and I am his: he feedeth among the lilies.
text.ASV: My beloved is mine, and I am his: He feedeth `his flock' among the lilies.
text.WEB: My beloved is mine, and I am his. He browses among the lilies.

text.KJV: Until the day break, and the shadows flee away, turn, my beloved, and be thou like a roe or a young hart upon the mountains of Bether.
text.ASV: Until the day be cool, and the shadows flee away, Turn, my beloved, and be thou like a roe or a young hart Upon the mountains of Bether.
text.WEB: Until the day is cool, and the shadows flee away, turn, my beloved, and be like a roe or a young deer on the mountains of Bether.

text.KJV: By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.
text.ASV: By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.
text.WEB: By night on my bed, I sought him whom my soul loves. I sought him, but I didn’t find him.

text.KJV: I will rise now, and go about the city in the streets, and in the broad ways I will seek him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.
text.ASV: `I said', I will rise now, and go about the city; In the streets and in the broad ways I will seek him whom my soul loveth: I sought him, but I found him not.
text.WEB: I will get up now, and go about the city; in the streets and in the squares I will seek him whom my soul loves. I sought him, but I didn’t find him.

text.KJV: The watchmen that go about the city found me: to whom I said, Saw ye him whom my soul loveth?
text.ASV: The watchmen that go about the city found me; `To whom I said', Saw ye him whom my soul loveth?
text.WEB: The watchmen who go about the city found me; “Have you seen him whom my soul loves?”

text.KJV: It was but a little that I passed from them, but I found him whom my soul loveth: I held him, and would not let him go, until I had brought him into my mother's house, and into the chamber of her that conceived me.
text.ASV: It was but a little that I passed from them, When I found him whom my soul loveth: I held him, and would not let him go, Until I had brought him into my mother's house, And into the chamber of her that conceived me.
text.WEB: I had scarcely passed from them, when I found him whom my soul loves. I held him, and would not let him go, until I had brought him into my mother’s house, into the room of her who conceived me.

text.KJV: I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please.
text.ASV: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, By the roes, or by the hinds of the field, That ye stir not up, nor awake `my' love, Until he please.
text.WEB: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, or by the hinds of the field, that you not stir up, nor awaken love, until it so desires.

text.KJV: Who is this that cometh out of the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all powders of the merchant?
text.ASV: Who is this that cometh up from the wilderness Like pillars of smoke, Perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, With all powders of the merchant?
text.WEB: Who is this who comes up from the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all spices of the merchant?

text.KJV: Behold his bed, which is Solomon's; threescore valiant men are about it, of the valiant of Israel.
text.ASV: Behold, it is the litter of Solomon; Threescore mighty men are about it, Of the mighty men of Israel.
text.WEB: Behold, it is Solomon’s carriage! Sixty mighty men are around it, of the mighty men of Israel.

text.KJV: They all hold swords, being expert in war: every man hath his sword upon his thigh because of fear in the night.
text.ASV: They all handle the sword, `and' are expert in war: Every man hath his sword upon his thigh, Because of fear in the night.
text.WEB: They all handle the sword, and are expert in war. Every man has his sword on his thigh, because of fear in the night.

text.KJV: King Solomon made himself a chariot of the wood of Lebanon.
text.ASV: King Solomon made himself a palanquin Of the wood of Lebanon.
text.WEB: King Solomon made himself a carriage of the wood of Lebanon.

text.KJV: He made the pillars thereof of silver, the bottom thereof of gold, the covering of it of purple, the midst thereof being paved with love, for the daughters of Jerusalem.
text.ASV: He made the pillars thereof of silver, The bottom thereof of gold, the seat of it of purple, The midst thereof being paved with love, From the daughters of Jerusalem.
text.WEB: He made its pillars of silver, its bottom of gold, its seat of purple, the middle of it being paved with love, from the daughters of Jerusalem.

text.KJV: Go forth, O ye daughters of Zion, and behold king Solomon with the crown wherewith his mother crowned him in the day of his espousals, and in the day of the gladness of his heart.
text.ASV: Go forth, O ye daughters of Zion, and behold king Solomon, With the crown wherewith his mother hath crowned him In the day of his espousals, And in the day of the gladness of his heart.
text.WEB: Go out, you daughters of Zion, and see king Solomon, with the crown with which his mother has crowned him, in the day of his weddings, in the day of the gladness of his heart.

text.KJV: Behold, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair; thou hast doves' eyes within thy locks: thy hair is as a flock of goats, that appear from mount Gilead.
text.ASV: Behold, thou art fair, my love; behold, thou art fair; Thine eyes are `as' doves behind thy veil. Thy hair is as a flock of goats, That lie along the side of mount Gilead.
text.WEB: Behold, you are beautiful, my love. Behold, you are beautiful. Your eyes are doves behind your veil. Your hair is as a flock of goats, that descend from Mount Gilead.

text.KJV: Thy teeth are like a flock of sheep that are even shorn, which came up from the washing; whereof every one bear twins, and none is barren among them.
text.ASV: Thy teeth are like a flock `of ewes' that are `newly' shorn, Which are come up from the washing, Whereof every one hath twins, And none is bereaved among them.
text.WEB: Your teeth are like a newly shorn flock, which have come up from the washing, where every one of them has twins. None is bereaved among them.

text.KJV: Thy lips are like a thread of scarlet, and thy speech is comely: thy temples are like a piece of a pomegranate within thy locks.
text.ASV: Thy lips are like a thread of scarlet, And thy mouth is comely. Thy temples are like a piece of a pomegranate Behind thy veil.
text.WEB: Your lips are like scarlet thread. Your mouth is lovely. Your temples are like a piece of a pomegranate behind your veil.

text.KJV: Thy neck is like the tower of David builded for an armoury, whereon there hang a thousand bucklers, all shields of mighty men.
text.ASV: Thy neck is like the tower of David builded for an armory, Whereon there hang a thousand bucklers, All the shields of the mighty men.
text.WEB: Your neck is like David’s tower built for an armory, whereon a thousand shields hang, all the shields of the mighty men.

text.KJV: Thy two breasts are like two young roes that are twins, which feed among the lilies.
text.ASV: Thy two breasts are like two fawns That are twins of a roe, Which feed among the lilies.
text.WEB: Your two breasts are like two fawns that are twins of a roe, which feed among the lilies.

text.KJV: Until the day break, and the shadows flee away, I will get me to the mountain of myrrh, and to the hill of frankincense.
text.ASV: Until the day be cool, and the shadows flee away, I will get me to the mountain of myrrh, And to the hill of frankincense.
text.WEB: Until the day is cool, and the shadows flee away, I will go to the mountain of myrrh, to the hill of frankincense.

text.KJV: Thou art all fair, my love; there is no spot in thee.
text.ASV: Thou art all fair, my love; And there is no spot in thee.
text.WEB: You are all beautiful, my love. There is no spot in you.

text.KJV: Come with me from Lebanon, my spouse, with me from Lebanon: look from the top of Amana, from the top of Shenir and Hermon, from the lions' dens, from the mountains of the leopards.
text.ASV: Come with me from Lebanon, `my' bride, With me from Lebanon: Look from the top of Amana, From the top of Senir and Hermon, From the lions' dens, From the mountains of the leopards.
text.WEB: Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, with me from Lebanon. Look from the top of Amana, from the top of Senir and Hermon, from the lions’ dens, from the mountains of the leopards.

text.KJV: Thou hast ravished my heart, my sister, my spouse; thou hast ravished my heart with one of thine eyes, with one chain of thy neck.
text.ASV: Thou hast ravished my heart, my sister, `my' bride; Thou hast ravished my heart with one of thine eyes, With one chain of thy neck.
text.WEB: You have ravished my heart, my sister, my bride. You have ravished my heart with one of your eyes, with one chain of your neck.

text.KJV: How fair is thy love, my sister, my spouse! how much better is thy love than wine! and the smell of thine ointments than all spices!
text.ASV: How fair is thy love, my sister, `my' bride! How much better is thy love than wine! And the fragrance of thine oils than all manner of spices!
text.WEB: How beautiful is your love, my sister, my bride! How much better is your love than wine! The fragrance of your perfumes than all kinds of spices!

text.KJV: Thy lips, O my spouse, drop as the honeycomb: honey and milk are under thy tongue; and the smell of thy garments is like the smell of Lebanon.
text.ASV: Thy lips, O `my' bride, drop `as' the honeycomb: Honey and milk are under thy tongue; And the smell of thy garments is like the smell of Lebanon.
text.WEB: Your lips, my bride, drip like the honeycomb. Honey and milk are under your tongue. The smell of your garments is like the smell of Lebanon.

text.KJV: A garden inclosed is my sister, my spouse; a spring shut up, a fountain sealed.
text.ASV: A garden shut up is my sister, `my' bride; A spring shut up, a fountain sealed.
text.WEB: A locked up garden is my sister, my bride; a locked up spring, a sealed fountain.

text.KJV: Thy plants are an orchard of pomegranates, with pleasant fruits; camphire, with spikenard,
text.ASV: Thy shoots are an orchard of pomegranates, with precious fruits; Henna with spikenard plants,
text.WEB: Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates, with precious fruits: henna with spikenard plants,

text.KJV: Spikenard and saffron; calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense; myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices:
text.ASV: Spikenard and saffron, Calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense; Myrrh and aloes, with all the chief spices.
text.WEB: spikenard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, with every kind of incense tree; myrrh and aloes, with all the best spices,

text.KJV: A fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, and streams from Lebanon.
text.ASV: `Thou art' a fountain of gardens, A well of living waters, And flowing streams from Lebanon.
text.WEB: a fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, flowing streams from Lebanon.

text.KJV: Awake, O north wind; and come, thou south; blow upon my garden, that the spices thereof may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and eat his pleasant fruits.
text.ASV: Awake, O north wind; and come, thou south; Blow upon my garden, that the spices thereof may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, And eat his precious fruits.
text.WEB: Awake, north wind; and come, you south! Blow on my garden, that its spices may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and taste his precious fruits.

text.KJV: I am come into my garden, my sister, my spouse: I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk: eat, O friends; drink, yea, drink abundantly, O beloved.
text.ASV: I am come into my garden, my sister, `my' bride: I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, O friends; Drink, yea, drink abundantly, O beloved.
text.WEB: I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride. I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Friends Eat, friends! Drink, yes, drink abundantly, beloved.

text.KJV: I sleep, but my heart waketh: it is the voice of my beloved that knocketh, saying, Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled: for my head is filled with dew, and my locks with the drops of the night.
text.ASV: I was asleep, but my heart waked: It is the voice of my beloved that knocketh, `saying', Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled; For my head is filled with dew, My locks with the drops of the night.
text.WEB: I was asleep, but my heart was awake. It is the voice of my beloved who knocks: “Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled; for my head is filled with dew, and my hair with the dampness of the night.”

text.KJV: I have put off my coat; how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet; how shall I defile them?
text.ASV: I have put off my garment; how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet; how shall I defile them?
text.WEB: I have taken off my robe. Indeed, must I put it on? I have washed my feet. Indeed, must I soil them?

text.KJV: My beloved put in his hand by the hole of the door, and my bowels were moved for him.
text.ASV: My beloved put in his hand by the hole `of the door', And my heart was moved for him.
text.WEB: My beloved thrust his hand in through the latch opening. My heart pounded for him.

text.KJV: I rose up to open to my beloved; and my hands dropped with myrrh, and my fingers with sweet smelling myrrh, upon the handles of the lock.
text.ASV: I rose up to open to my beloved; And my hands droppeth with myrrh, And my fingers with liquid myrrh, Upon the handles of the bolt.
text.WEB: I rose up to open for my beloved. My hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with liquid myrrh, on the handles of the lock.

text.KJV: I opened to my beloved; but my beloved had withdrawn himself, and was gone: my soul failed when he spake: I sought him, but I could not find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer.
text.ASV: I opened to my beloved; But my beloved had withdrawn himself, `and' was gone. My soul had failed me when he spake: I sought him, but I could not find him; I called him, but he gave me no answer.
text.WEB: I opened to my beloved; but my beloved left; and had gone away. My heart went out when he spoke. I looked for him, but I didn’t find him. I called him, but he didn’t answer.

text.KJV: The watchmen that went about the city found me, they smote me, they wounded me; the keepers of the walls took away my veil from me.
text.ASV: The watchmen that go about the city found me, They smote me, they wounded me; The keepers of the walls took away my mantle from me.
text.WEB: The watchmen who go about the city found me. They beat me. They bruised me. The keepers of the walls took my cloak away from me.

text.KJV: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, if ye find my beloved, that ye tell him, that I am sick of love.
text.ASV: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, If ye find my beloved, That ye tell him, that I am sick from love.
text.WEB: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, If you find my beloved, that you tell him that I am faint with love.

text.KJV: What is thy beloved more than another beloved, O thou fairest among women? what is thy beloved more than another beloved, that thou dost so charge us?
text.ASV: What is thy beloved more than `another' beloved, O thou fairest among women? What is thy beloved more than `another' beloved, That thou dost so adjure us?
text.WEB: How is your beloved better than another beloved, you fairest among women? How is your beloved better than another beloved, that you do so adjure us?

text.KJV: My beloved is white and ruddy, the chiefest among ten thousand.
text.ASV: My beloved is white and ruddy, The chiefest among ten thousand.
text.WEB: My beloved is white and ruddy. The best among ten thousand.

text.KJV: His head is as the most fine gold, his locks are bushy, and black as a raven.
text.ASV: His head is `as' the most fine gold; His locks are bushy, `and' black as a raven.
text.WEB: His head is like the purest gold. His hair is bushy, black as a raven.

text.KJV: His eyes are as the eyes of doves by the rivers of waters, washed with milk, and fitly set.
text.ASV: His eyes are like doves beside the water-brooks, Washed with milk, `and' fitly set.
text.WEB: His eyes are like doves beside the water brooks, washed with milk, mounted like jewels.

text.KJV: His cheeks are as a bed of spices, as sweet flowers: his lips like lilies, dropping sweet smelling myrrh.
text.ASV: His cheeks are as a bed of spices, `As' banks of sweet herbs: His lips are `as' lilies, dropping liquid myrrh.
text.WEB: His cheeks are like a bed of spices with towers of perfumes. His lips are like lilies, dropping liquid myrrh.

text.KJV: His hands are as gold rings set with the beryl: his belly is as bright ivory overlaid with sapphires.
text.ASV: His hands are `as' rings of gold set with beryl: His body is `as' ivory work overlaid `with' sapphires.
text.WEB: His hands are like rings of gold set with beryl. His body is like ivory work overlaid with sapphires.

text.KJV: His legs are as pillars of marble, set upon sockets of fine gold: his countenance is as Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.
text.ASV: His legs are `as' pillars of marble, set upon sockets of fine gold: His aspect is like Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.
text.WEB: His legs are like pillars of marble set on sockets of fine gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.

text.KJV: His mouth is most sweet: yea, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.
text.ASV: His mouth is most sweet; Yea, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, O daughters of Jerusalem.
text.WEB: His mouth is sweetness; yes, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, daughters of Jerusalem.

text.KJV: Whither is thy beloved gone, O thou fairest among women? whither is thy beloved turned aside? that we may seek him with thee.
text.ASV: Whither is thy beloved gone, O thou fairest among women? Whither hath thy beloved turned him, That we may seek him with thee?
text.WEB: Where has your beloved gone, you fairest among women? Where has your beloved turned, that we may seek him with you?

text.KJV: My beloved is gone down into his garden, to the beds of spices, to feed in the gardens, and to gather lilies.
text.ASV: My beloved is gone down to his garden, To the beds of spices, To feed in the gardens, and to gather lilies.
text.WEB: My beloved has gone down to his garden, to the beds of spices, to feed in the gardens, and to gather lilies.

text.KJV: I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine: he feedeth among the lilies.
text.ASV: I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine; He feedeth `his flock' among the lilies,
text.WEB: I am my beloved’s, and my beloved is mine. He browses among the lilies,

text.KJV: Thou art beautiful, O my love, as Tirzah, comely as Jerusalem, terrible as an army with banners.
text.ASV: Thou art fair, O my love, as Tirzah, Comely as Jerusalem, Terrible as an army with banners.
text.WEB: You are beautiful, my love, as Tirzah, lovely as Jerusalem, awesome as an army with banners.

text.KJV: Turn away thine eyes from me, for they have overcome me: thy hair is as a flock of goats that appear from Gilead.
text.ASV: Turn away thine eyes from me, For they have overcome me. Thy hair is as a flock of goats, That lie along the side of Gilead.
text.WEB: Turn away your eyes from me, for they have overcome me. Your hair is like a flock of goats, that lie along the side of Gilead.

text.KJV: Thy teeth are as a flock of sheep which go up from the washing, whereof every one beareth twins, and there is not one barren among them.
text.ASV: Thy teeth are like a flock of ewes, Which are come up from the washing; Whereof every one hath twins, And none is bereaved among them.
text.WEB: Your teeth are like a flock of ewes, which have come up from the washing; of which every one has twins; no one is bereaved among them.

text.KJV: As a piece of a pomegranate are thy temples within thy locks.
text.ASV: Thy temples are like a piece of a pomegranate Behind thy veil.
text.WEB: Your temples are like a piece of a pomegranate behind your veil.

text.KJV: There are threescore queens, and fourscore concubines, and virgins without number.
text.ASV: There are threescore queens, and fourscore concubines, And virgins without number.
text.WEB: There are sixty queens, eighty concubines, and virgins without number.

text.KJV: My dove, my undefiled is but one; she is the only one of her mother, she is the choice one of her that bare her. The daughters saw her, and blessed her; yea, the queens and the concubines, and they praised her.
text.ASV: My dove, my undefiled, is `but' one; She is the only one of her mother; She is the choice one of her that bare her. The daughters saw her, and called her blessed; `Yea', the queens and the concubines, and they praised her.
text.WEB: My dove, my perfect one, is unique. She is her mother’s only daughter. She is the favorite one of her who bore her. The daughters saw her, and called her blessed; the queens and the concubines, and they praised her.

text.KJV: Who is she that looketh forth as the morning, fair as the moon, clear as the sun, and terrible as an army with banners?
text.ASV: Who is she that looketh forth as the morning, Fair as the moon, Clear as the sun, Terrible as an army with banners?
text.WEB: Who is she who looks out as the morning, beautiful as the moon, clear as the sun, and awesome as an army with banners?

text.KJV: I went down into the garden of nuts to see the fruits of the valley, and to see whether the vine flourished and the pomegranates budded.
text.ASV: I went down into the garden of nuts, To see the green plants of the valley, To see whether the vine budded, `And' the pomegranates were in flower.
text.WEB: I went down into the nut tree grove, to see the green plants of the valley, to see whether the vine budded, and the pomegranates were in flower.

text.KJV: Or ever I was aware, my soul made me like the chariots of Amminadib.
text.ASV: Before I was aware, my soul set me `Among' the chariots of my princely people.
text.WEB: Without realizing it, my desire set me with my royal people’s chariots.

text.KJV: Return, return, O Shulamite; return, return, that we may look upon thee. What will ye see in the Shulamite? As it were the company of two armies.
text.ASV: Return, return, O Shulammite; Return, return, that we may look upon thee. Why will ye look upon the Shulammite, As upon the dance of Mahanaim?
text.WEB: Return, return, Shulammite! Return, return, that we may gaze at you. Lover Why do you desire to gaze at the Shulammite, as at the dance of Mahanaim?

text.KJV: How beautiful are thy feet with shoes, O prince's daughter! the joints of thy thighs are like jewels, the work of the hands of a cunning workman.
text.ASV: How beautiful are thy feet in sandals, O prince's daughter! Thy rounded thighs are like jewels, The work of the hands of a skilful workman.
text.WEB: How beautiful are your feet in sandals, prince’s daughter! Your rounded thighs are like jewels, the work of the hands of a skillful workman.

text.KJV: Thy navel is like a round goblet, which wanteth not liquor: thy belly is like an heap of wheat set about with lilies.
text.ASV: Thy body is `like' a round goblet, `Wherein' no mingled wine is wanting: Thy waist is `like' a heap of wheat Set about with lilies.
text.WEB: Your body is like a round goblet, no mixed wine is wanting. Your waist is like a heap of wheat, set about with lilies.

text.KJV: Thy two breasts are like two young roes that are twins.
text.ASV: Thy two breasts are like two fawns That are twins of a roe.
text.WEB: Your two breasts are like two fawns, that are twins of a roe.

text.KJV: Thy neck is as a tower of ivory; thine eyes like the fishpools in Heshbon, by the gate of Bathrabbim: thy nose is as the tower of Lebanon which looketh toward Damascus.
text.ASV: Thy neck is like the tower of ivory; Thine eyes `as' the pools in Heshbon, By the gate of Bath-rabbim; Thy nose is like the tower of Lebanon Which looketh toward Damascus.
text.WEB: Your neck is like an ivory tower. Your eyes are like the pools in Heshbon by the gate of Bathrabbim. Your nose is like the tower of Lebanon which looks toward Damascus.

text.KJV: Thine head upon thee is like Carmel, and the hair of thine head like purple; the king is held in the galleries.
text.ASV: Thy head upon thee is like Carmel, And the hair of thy head like purple; The king is held captive in the tresses `thereof'.
text.WEB: Your head on you is like Carmel. The hair of your head like purple. The king is held captive in its tresses.

text.KJV: How fair and how pleasant art thou, O love, for delights!
text.ASV: How fair and how pleasant art thou, O love, for delights!
text.WEB: How beautiful and how pleasant you are, love, for delights!

text.KJV: This thy stature is like to a palm tree, and thy breasts to clusters of grapes.
text.ASV: This thy stature is like to a palm-tree, And thy breasts to its clusters.
text.WEB: This, your stature, is like a palm tree, your breasts like its fruit.

text.KJV: I said, I will go up to the palm tree, I will take hold of the boughs thereof: now also thy breasts shall be as clusters of the vine, and the smell of thy nose like apples;
text.ASV: I said, I will climb up into the palm-tree, I will take hold of the branches thereof: Let thy breasts be as clusters of the vine, And the smell of thy breath like apples,
text.WEB: I said, “I will climb up into the palm tree. I will take hold of its fruit.” Let your breasts be like clusters of the vine, the smell of your breath like apples,

text.KJV: And the roof of thy mouth like the best wine for my beloved, that goeth down sweetly, causing the lips of those that are asleep to speak.
text.ASV: And thy mouth like the best wine, That goeth down smoothly for my beloved, Gliding through the lips of those that are asleep.
text.WEB: Your mouth like the best wine, that goes down smoothly for my beloved, gliding through the lips of those who are asleep.

text.KJV: I am my beloved's, and his desire is toward me.
text.ASV: I am my beloved's; And his desire is toward me.
text.WEB: I am my beloved’s. His desire is toward me.

text.KJV: Come, my beloved, let us go forth into the field; let us lodge in the villages.
text.ASV: Come, my beloved, let us go forth into the field; Let us lodge in the villages.
text.WEB: Come, my beloved, let us go out into the field. Let us lodge in the villages.

text.KJV: Let us get up early to the vineyards; let us see if the vine flourish, whether the tender grape appear, and the pomegranates bud forth: there will I give thee my loves.
text.ASV: Let us get up early to the vineyards; Let us see whether the vine hath budded, `And' its blossom is open, `And' the pomegranates are in flower: There will I give thee my love.
text.WEB: Let’s go early up to the vineyards. Let’s see whether the vine has budded, its blossom is open, and the pomegranates are in flower. There I will give you my love.

text.KJV: The mandrakes give a smell, and at our gates are all manner of pleasant fruits, new and old, which I have laid up for thee, O my beloved.
text.ASV: The mandrakes give forth fragrance; And at our doors are all manner of precious fruits, new and old, Which I have laid up for thee, O my beloved.
text.WEB: The mandrakes produce fragrance. At our doors are all kinds of precious fruits, new and old, which I have stored up for you, my beloved.

text.KJV: O that thou wert as my brother, that sucked the breasts of my mother! when I should find thee without, I would kiss thee; yea, I should not be despised.
text.ASV: Oh that thou wert as my brother, That sucked the breasts of my mother! `When' I should find thee without, I would kiss thee; Yea, and none would despise me.
text.WEB: Oh that you were like my brother, who nursed from the breasts of my mother! If I found you outside, I would kiss you; yes, and no one would despise me.

text.KJV: I would lead thee, and bring thee into my mother's house, who would instruct me: I would cause thee to drink of spiced wine of the juice of my pomegranate.
text.ASV: I would lead thee, `and' bring thee into my mother's house, Who would instruct me; I would cause thee to drink of spiced wine, Of the juice of my pomegranate.
text.WEB: I would lead you, bringing you into my mother’s house, who would instruct me. I would have you drink spiced wine, of the juice of my pomegranate.

text.KJV: His left hand should be under my head, and his right hand should embrace me.
text.ASV: His left hand `should be' under my head, And his right hand should embrace me.
text.WEB: His left hand would be under my head. His right hand would embrace me.

text.KJV: I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem, that ye stir not up, nor awake my love, until he please.
text.ASV: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, That ye stir not up, nor awake `my' love, Until he please.
text.WEB: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, that you not stir up, nor awaken love, until it so desires.

text.KJV: Who is this that cometh up from the wilderness, leaning upon her beloved? I raised thee up under the apple tree: there thy mother brought thee forth: there she brought thee forth that bare thee.
text.ASV: Who is this that cometh up from the wilderness, Leaning upon her beloved? Under the apple-tree I awakened thee: There thy mother was in travail with thee, There was she in travail that brought thee forth.
text.WEB: Who is this who comes up from the wilderness, leaning on her beloved? Under the apple tree I aroused you. There your mother conceived you. There she was in labor and bore you.

text.KJV: Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm: for love is strong as death; jealousy is cruel as the grave: the coals thereof are coals of fire, which hath a most vehement flame.
text.ASV: Set me as a seal upon thy heart, As a seal upon thine arm: For love is strong as death; Jealousy is cruel as Sheol; The flashes thereof are flashes of fire, A very flame of Jehovah.
text.WEB: Set me as a seal on your heart, as a seal on your arm; for love is strong as death. Jealousy is as cruel as Sheol. Its flashes are flashes of fire, a very flame of Yahweh.

text.KJV: Many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it: if a man would give all the substance of his house for love, it would utterly be contemned.
text.ASV: Many waters cannot quench love, Neither can floods drown it: If a man would give all the substance of his house for love, He would utterly be contemned.
text.WEB: Many waters can’t quench love, neither can floods drown it. If a man would give all the wealth of his house for love, he would be utterly scorned.

text.KJV: We have a little sister, and she hath no breasts: what shall we do for our sister in the day when she shall be spoken for?
text.ASV: We have a little sister, And she hath no breasts: What shall we do for our sister In the day when she shall be spoken for?
text.WEB: We have a little sister. She has no breasts. What shall we do for our sister in the day when she is to be spoken for?

text.KJV: If she be a wall, we will build upon her a palace of silver: and if she be a door, we will inclose her with boards of cedar.
text.ASV: If she be a wall, We will build upon her a turret of silver: And if she be a door, We will inclose her with boards of cedar.
text.WEB: If she is a wall, we will build on her a turret of silver. if she is a door, we will enclose her with boards of cedar.

text.KJV: I am a wall, and my breasts like towers: then was I in his eyes as one that found favour.
text.ASV: I am a wall, and my breasts like the towers `thereof' Then was I in his eyes as one that found peace.
text.WEB: I am a wall, and my breasts like towers, then I was in his eyes like one who found peace.

text.KJV: Solomon had a vineyard at Baalhamon; he let out the vineyard unto keepers; every one for the fruit thereof was to bring a thousand pieces of silver.
text.ASV: Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon; He let out the vineyard unto keepers; Every one for the fruit thereof was to bring a thousand `pieces' of silver.
text.WEB: Solomon had a vineyard at Baal Hamon. He leased out the vineyard to keepers. Each was to bring a thousand shekels of silver for its fruit.

text.KJV: My vineyard, which is mine, is before me: thou, O Solomon, must have a thousand, and those that keep the fruit thereof two hundred.
text.ASV: My vineyard, which is mine, is before me: Thou, O Solomon, shalt have the thousand, And those that keep the fruit thereof two hundred.
text.WEB: My own vineyard is before me. The thousand are for you, Solomon; two hundred for those who tend its fruit.

text.KJV: Thou that dwellest in the gardens, the companions hearken to thy voice: cause me to hear it.
text.ASV: Thou that dwellest in the gardens, The companions hearken for thy voice: Cause me to hear it.
text.WEB: You who dwell in the gardens, with friends in attendance, let me hear your voice!

text.KJV: Make haste, my beloved, and be thou like to a roe or to a young hart upon the mountains of spices.
text.ASV: Make haste, my beloved, And be thou like to a roe or to a young hart Upon the mountains of spices.
text.WEB: Come away, my beloved! Be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of spices!
